people.jeremiah.relations: He is Hilkiah’s son, from the priests of Anathoth. Baruch writes his words, and Judah’s officials jail him.
people.jeremiah.meaning: God calls him when he says he is too young to speak. He warns the temple crowd, and Pashhur puts him in stocks. Officials throw him in a pit, and Ebedmelech pulls him out. After the city falls, survivors take him to Egypt.
people.hilkiah-father.relations: He is Jeremiah’s father and one of the priests in Anathoth.
people.hilkiah-father.meaning: The first verse names him as Jeremiah’s father. He is one of the priests in Anathoth in Benjamin. The book does not say he is the high priest of Josiah’s time.
people.josiah.relations: He is Amon’s son. Jehoiakim, Shallum, and Zedekiah are his sons.
people.josiah.meaning: God’s word first comes to Jeremiah in his thirteenth year as king. Later Jeremiah reminds Jehoiakim of him. Josiah did what was fair and judged the cause of the poor. Jeremiah says it went well with him then.
people.amon-king.role: Josiah’s father, named in two dates
people.amon-king.meaning: The book names him only as Josiah’s father. His name appears where the book dates Jeremiah’s first message. He does nothing in this book.
people.jehoiakim.meaning: Jeremiah says he builds his house with workers he does not pay. He has the prophet Uriah brought back from Egypt and kills him. Jehudi reads him Jeremiah’s scroll. He cuts it up and burns it, though three officials beg him not to.
people.zedekiah.role: King who asks Jeremiah in secret but will not surrender
people.zedekiah.relations: He is Josiah’s son, and Hamutal is his mother. Nebuchadnezzar makes him king, then captures and blinds him.
people.zedekiah.meaning: He sends men to ask Jeremiah for help against Babylon. He lets the officials put Jeremiah in a pit, then lets Ebedmelech save him. Jeremiah tells him to give himself up, but he fears being mocked. He runs at night and is caught near Jericho.
people.nebuchadnezzar.relations: He makes Zedekiah king and later judges him at Riblah. He tells Nebuzaradan to take care of Jeremiah.
people.nebuchadnezzar.meaning: God calls him “my servant” and gives the nations into his hand. His army surrounds Jerusalem and breaks in. At Riblah he kills Zedekiah’s sons and puts out Zedekiah’s eyes. The book also says Babylon will be punished in its turn.
people.jehoiachin.relations: He is Jehoiakim’s son. His mother and the princes of Judah go to Babylon with him.
people.jehoiachin.meaning: The book also calls him Jeconiah and Coniah. Jeremiah says God will cast him and his mother into another land. Nebuchadnezzar carries him to Babylon. In the thirty-seventh year, Evilmerodach frees him from prison and feeds him each day.
people.jehoahaz-judah.role: Josiah’s son who is led away and will not return
people.jehoahaz-judah.relations: He is Josiah’s son and became king after him.
people.jehoahaz-judah.meaning: Jeremiah calls him Shallum. He became king after Josiah and then was led away captive. Jeremiah tells the people to weep for him, not for the dead. He will die where he was taken and not see his land again.
people.david.role: Earlier king whose family is promised a fair ruler
people.david.relations: Jeremiah calls Judah’s royal family the house of David.
people.david.meaning: Jeremiah tells the house of David to do justice every morning. God promises to raise a righteous Branch for David. That king will rule fairly, and Judah will be safe. God says David will never lack a man on the throne.
people.manasseh-king.role: Earlier king whose acts God blames
people.manasseh-king.relations: He is Hezekiah’s son and a king of Judah.
people.manasseh-king.meaning: God says he will toss Judah among all the kingdoms. He gives the reason: what Manasseh did in Jerusalem. The verse does not list those acts.
people.moses.role: Earlier leader God names with Samuel
people.moses.meaning: God says he would not turn toward Judah even if Moses stood before him. Moses does nothing else in this book. God names him to show that no one’s plea will help now.
people.samuel.meaning: God says he would not turn toward Judah even if Samuel stood before him. Samuel does nothing else in this book. His name shows that pleading for Judah will not work now.
people.rachel.role: Mother heard weeping for her children in Ramah
people.rachel.relations: The poem calls the lost people her children.
people.rachel.meaning: A voice is heard in Ramah. Rachel weeps for her children and will not be comforted, because they are gone. God tells her to stop weeping. He says her children will come back from the enemy’s land.
people.baruch.relations: He is Neriah’s son. He writes for Jeremiah, and Johanan’s group takes both men to Egypt.
people.baruch.meaning: He stores the deeds for Jeremiah’s field in a clay jar. He writes Jeremiah’s words on a scroll and reads it at the temple. After the king burns it, he writes it again. When he complains of sorrow, God promises him his life.
people.pashhur-immer.relations: He is the son of Immer the priest. He is not Pashhur the son of Malchijah.
people.pashhur-immer.meaning: He hears Jeremiah’s warning and strikes him. He locks him in the stocks at the upper gate of Benjamin. The next day he lets him go. Jeremiah gives him a new name, Magormissabib, and says he will die in Babylon.
people.pashhur-malchijah.role: Official sent to Jeremiah who later asks for his death
people.pashhur-malchijah.relations: He is Malchijah’s son. He is not Pashhur the son of Immer.
people.pashhur-malchijah.meaning: Zedekiah sends him with Zephaniah to ask Jeremiah for God’s help against Babylon. Later he hears Jeremiah tell the people to go out to the Chaldeans. He and three other officials ask the king to put Jeremiah to death.
people.zephaniah-priest.role: Priest who carries the king’s requests to Jeremiah
people.zephaniah-priest.relations: He is Maaseiah’s son and the second priest. The king of Babylon kills him at Riblah.
people.zephaniah-priest.meaning: Zedekiah sends him to Jeremiah twice, once to ask for help and once for prayer. Shemaiah writes to him and asks why he has not punished Jeremiah. Zephaniah reads that letter to Jeremiah. After the city falls, Nebuzaradan takes him to Riblah.
people.hananiah-azzur.role: Prophet who says Babylon’s rule will end in two years
people.hananiah-azzur.relations: He is Azzur’s son, from Gibeon. He speaks against Jeremiah in the temple.
people.hananiah-azzur.meaning: He says God will bring back the temple vessels and the captives within two years. He takes the wooden bar off Jeremiah’s neck and breaks it. Jeremiah tells him God did not send him and he will die that year. He dies in the seventh month.
people.uriah-shemaiah.role: Prophet killed for warnings like Jeremiah’s
people.uriah-shemaiah.relations: He is Shemaiah’s son, from Kiriath Jearim. Jehoiakim sends Elnathan to bring him back from Egypt.
people.uriah-shemaiah.meaning: He speaks against the city and the land, as Jeremiah does. Jehoiakim wants him dead, so he flees to Egypt. The king’s men bring him back. Jehoiakim kills him with the sword and throws his body among the common graves.
people.micah-prophet.relations: He spoke in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
people.micah-prophet.meaning: Some elders quote him at Jeremiah’s hearing. Micah said Zion would be plowed like a field. Hezekiah did not kill him for it. The elders use this to argue that Jeremiah should live.
people.hezekiah.relations: Micah spoke in his days. Manasseh is named as his son.
people.hezekiah.meaning: The elders recall how he heard Micah’s warning. He did not put Micah to death. He feared the LORD and asked for his favor, and the disaster did not come. The elders set this beside the call to kill Jeremiah.
people.ahikam.role: Official who keeps Jeremiah from being killed
people.ahikam.meaning: The crowd at the temple wants Jeremiah dead. Ahikam stands with Jeremiah, so he is not handed over to the people. Later the book names him as the father of Gedaliah.
people.shaphan.role: Father of several officials who help Jeremiah
people.shaphan.relations: Ahikam, Elasah, and Gemariah are named as his sons. Gedaliah and Micaiah are his grandsons.
people.shaphan.meaning: Shaphan does nothing himself in this book. His son Ahikam protects Jeremiah. His son Elasah carries Jeremiah’s letter to Babylon. Baruch reads the scroll in the room of his son Gemariah.
people.elnathan-achbor.role: Official who brings Uriah back and later defends the scroll
people.elnathan-achbor.relations: He is Achbor’s son. He serves King Jehoiakim.
people.elnathan-achbor.meaning: Jehoiakim sends him to Egypt with men to bring back Uriah. Uriah is then killed. Later he hears Baruch read the scroll. He begs the king not to burn it, but the king does not listen.
people.elasah-shaphan.relations: He is Shaphan’s son. He travels with Gemariah the son of Hilkiah.
people.elasah-shaphan.meaning: Zedekiah sends him to Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon. He carries Jeremiah’s letter to the captives there. The letter tells them to build houses and plant gardens. He appears only in this verse.
people.gemariah-hilkiah.relations: He is Hilkiah’s son. He is not Gemariah the son of Shaphan.
people.gemariah-hilkiah.meaning: Zedekiah sends him to Babylon with Elasah. The two carry Jeremiah’s letter to the captives. The text does not say which Hilkiah is his father.
people.ahab-kolaiah.role: Prophet in Babylon whom Jeremiah says lies
people.ahab-kolaiah.relations: He is Kolaiah’s son. Jeremiah names him beside Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah.
people.ahab-kolaiah.meaning: Jeremiah’s letter says he tells lies in God’s name. It also charges him with adultery with his neighbors’ wives. God will hand him to Nebuchadnezzar, who will kill him in front of the captives. The captives will use his name in a curse.
people.zedekiah-maaseiah.role: Prophet in Babylon whom Jeremiah says lies
people.zedekiah-maaseiah.relations: He is Maaseiah’s son. He is not King Zedekiah.
people.zedekiah-maaseiah.meaning: Jeremiah’s letter names him with Ahab as a lying prophet in Babylon. It charges both with adultery with their neighbors’ wives. God will hand them to Nebuchadnezzar to be killed. A curse will recall that the king roasted them in the fire.
people.shemaiah-nehelamite.role: Man in Babylon who writes to have Jeremiah punished
people.shemaiah-nehelamite.relations: He writes to Zephaniah the priest and to the people in Jerusalem.
people.shemaiah-nehelamite.meaning: He hears Jeremiah’s message that the captivity will be long. He writes to Zephaniah and asks why Jeremiah is not in the stocks. Jeremiah answers that God did not send Shemaiah. None of his family will see the good God will do.
people.hanamel.relations: He is the son of Shallum, Jeremiah’s uncle.
people.hanamel.meaning: He comes to Jeremiah in the court of the guard. He asks Jeremiah to buy his field in Anathoth. Jeremiah pays seventeen shekels of silver and signs the deed. God says houses and fields will be bought in this land again.
people.rechabites.role: Family who will not drink wine
people.rechabites.relations: They call Jonadab the son of Rechab their father. Jaazaniah is named with them.
people.rechabites.meaning: Jeremiah brings them to a temple room and sets wine before them. They refuse, because Jonadab told them never to drink wine. They also live in tents, as he said. God sets them beside Judah, who has not listened to him.
people.jaazaniah-rechabite.role: Rechabite whom Jeremiah brings to the temple
people.jaazaniah-rechabite.relations: He is the son of another Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah.
people.jaazaniah-rechabite.meaning: Jeremiah takes him, his brothers, and his sons to the temple. The whole house of the Rechabites comes too. The text names him first but gives him no words of his own.
people.jehonadab.role: Father whose rules the Rechabites keep
people.jehonadab.relations: He is Rechab’s son. The Rechabites call him their father.
people.jehonadab.meaning: He told his family never to drink wine. He told them to build no houses and to live in tents. In Jeremiah’s day they still obey. God promises that Jonadab will always have a man to stand before him.
people.gemariah-shaphan.role: Official whose temple room Baruch reads in
people.gemariah-shaphan.relations: He is the son of Shaphan the scribe. Micaiah is his son.
people.gemariah-shaphan.meaning: Baruch reads the scroll to the people in his room at the temple. His son Micaiah tells the officials what he heard. Gemariah hears the scroll with them. He begs the king not to burn it, but the king will not listen.
people.micaiah-gemariah.role: Listener who tells the officials what Baruch read
people.micaiah-gemariah.relations: He is the son of Gemariah and the grandson of Shaphan.
people.micaiah-gemariah.meaning: He hears Baruch read the scroll at the temple. He goes down to the king’s house and tells the officials. They send for Baruch, and the scroll reaches the king.
people.elishama-scribe.role: Scribe whose room holds the scroll
people.elishama-scribe.relations: He sits with the officials who hear Baruch.
people.elishama-scribe.meaning: He is with the officials when Micaiah brings news of the scroll. They hear Baruch read it. They leave the scroll in his room and go to tell the king. Jehudi takes it from there to read to the king.
people.delaiah-shemaiah.relations: He is Shemaiah’s son. He joins Elnathan and Gemariah in asking the king.
people.delaiah-shemaiah.meaning: He sits with the officials who hear Baruch read the scroll. They tell Baruch and Jeremiah to hide. He asks the king not to burn the scroll. The king does not listen.
people.zedekiah-hananiah.role: Official who sits with the princes in the scribe’s room
people.zedekiah-hananiah.relations: He is Hananiah’s son. He is not King Zedekiah.
people.zedekiah-hananiah.meaning: He sits with the officials when Micaiah reports Baruch’s reading. The text names him once and gives him no act of his own.
people.jehudi.relations: He is the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi.
people.jehudi.meaning: The officials send him to bring Baruch and the scroll. Later the king sends him to get the scroll from Elishama’s room. He reads three or four columns to the king. The king cuts the scroll and burns it all.
people.arrest-officers.role: Three men the king sends to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch
people.arrest-officers.relations: Jerahmeel is called the king’s son. Seraiah is Azriel’s son, and Shelemiah is Abdeel’s son.
people.arrest-officers.meaning: After he burns the scroll, Jehoiakim tells these three to seize Baruch and Jeremiah. They do not find them. The text says the LORD hid them.
people.jehucal-shelemiah.role: Official who asks for prayer and later for Jeremiah’s death
people.jehucal-shelemiah.relations: He is Shelemiah’s son. Zedekiah sends him with Zephaniah the priest.
people.jehucal-shelemiah.meaning: Zedekiah sends him to ask Jeremiah to pray for the people. Later he hears Jeremiah tell the people to go out to the Chaldeans. He joins the officials who ask the king to kill Jeremiah. The text spells his name Jehucal and Jucal.
people.irijah.role: Guard captain who arrests Jeremiah at the gate
people.irijah.relations: He is the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah.
people.irijah.meaning: He stops Jeremiah at Benjamin’s gate and says he is going over to the Chaldeans. Jeremiah says that is false. Irijah does not listen and takes him to the officials. They beat Jeremiah and put him in prison.
people.jonathan-scribe.role: Scribe whose house becomes Jeremiah’s prison
people.jonathan-scribe.relations: The text calls him the scribe. He is not Jonathan the son of Kareah.
people.jonathan-scribe.meaning: The officials make his house the prison and put Jeremiah in its cells. Jeremiah stays there many days. He begs Zedekiah not to send him back, or he will die there. Jonathan himself does not act or speak.
people.hostile-officials.role: Two officials who ask the king to kill Jeremiah
people.hostile-officials.relations: Shephatiah is Mattan’s son. Gedaliah is Pashhur’s son, and is not Gedaliah the governor.
people.hostile-officials.meaning: They hear Jeremiah tell the people to go out to the Chaldeans and live. With Jucal and Pashhur, they tell the king he weakens the soldiers. The king gives Jeremiah into their hands. They lower him into a pit of mud.
people.malchijah-royal.role: King’s son whose pit holds Jeremiah
people.malchijah-royal.relations: He is called the king’s son. The text does not say he is Pashhur’s father.
people.malchijah-royal.meaning: The officials throw Jeremiah into his pit in the court of the guard. The pit has no water, only mud, and Jeremiah sinks in it. Malchijah himself does nothing in the story.
people.ebedmelech.relations: He is an Ethiopian who serves in King Zedekiah’s house.
people.ebedmelech.meaning: He hears that Jeremiah is in the pit and warns the king he will die. The king gives him thirty men. He lowers old rags for Jeremiah to pad the ropes, then pulls him out. God promises Ebedmelech that he will live when the city falls.
people.babylonian-officers.role: Babylonian officials who sit in the gate and free Jeremiah
people.babylonian-officers.relations: Verse 3 lists Nergal Sharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, and a second Nergal Sharezer. Verse 13 names Nebushazban and Nergal Sharezer with Nebuzaradan.
people.babylonian-officers.meaning: They enter Jerusalem when the wall is broken and sit in the middle gate. Later they send for Jeremiah and take him out of the court of the guard. They hand him to Gedaliah. The text does not say if the two Nergal Sharezer names are one man.
people.nebuzaradan.role: Babylonian captain who burns the city and frees Jeremiah
people.nebuzaradan.relations: He is Nebuchadnezzar’s captain of the guard. He leaves the remaining people with Gedaliah.
people.nebuzaradan.meaning: He burns the temple, the king’s house, and the houses of Jerusalem. He carries people to Babylon and leaves the poorest to farm. At Ramah he takes off Jeremiah’s chains and lets him choose where to go. He takes Seraiah and Zephaniah to Riblah.
people.gedaliah.relations: He is Ahikam’s son and Shaphan’s grandson. He is not Gedaliah the son of Pashhur.
people.gedaliah.meaning: The king of Babylon makes him governor, and he lives at Mizpah. He tells the commanders to serve Babylon and gather wine, fruit, and oil. Johanan warns him about Ishmael, but he does not believe it. Ishmael kills him at a meal in Mizpah.
people.ishmael-nethaniah.role: Man of the royal family who kills Gedaliah
people.ishmael-nethaniah.relations: He is the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama. Johanan says Baalis sent him.
people.ishmael-nethaniah.meaning: He eats with Gedaliah at Mizpah, then kills him with ten men. Two days later he kills most of eighty men who come with offerings. He takes the people of Mizpah captive and heads for Ammon. Johanan catches him at Gibeon, and he escapes with eight men.
people.johanan-kareah.role: Commander who warns Gedaliah and later leads the people to Egypt
people.johanan-kareah.relations: He is Kareah’s son and Jonathan’s brother. He warns Gedaliah, fights Ishmael, and argues with Jeremiah.
people.johanan-kareah.meaning: He tells Gedaliah that Ishmael plans to kill him and offers to kill Ishmael first. After the murder he frees Ishmael’s captives at Gibeon. He asks Jeremiah to pray, calls the answer a lie, and leads all to Egypt.
people.jonathan-kareah.relations: He is Kareah’s son and Johanan’s brother. He is not Jonathan the scribe.
people.jonathan-kareah.meaning: He comes with his brother and the other commanders to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells them to serve the king of Babylon. The text names him only here.
people.seraiah-captain.relations: He is Tanhumeth’s son. He is not Seraiah the son of Neriah or Seraiah the chief priest.
people.seraiah-captain.meaning: He comes with his men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells the commanders not to fear serving the Chaldeans. The text names him only in this list.
people.jezaniah-maacathite.relations: The text calls him the son of the Maacathite. It does not link him with Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah.
people.jezaniah-maacathite.meaning: He comes with his men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells the commanders to gather wine, summer fruits, and oil. The text names him only in this list.
people.baalis.role: Ammonite king whom Johanan accuses of sending Ishmael
people.baalis.relations: He is king of the children of Ammon. Johanan links him with Ishmael.
people.baalis.meaning: Johanan tells Gedaliah that Baalis has sent Ishmael to kill him. Gedaliah does not believe it. The text gives only Johanan’s report. Later Ishmael does kill Gedaliah and flees toward Ammon.
people.jezaniah-hoshaiah.relations: He is Hoshaiah’s son and stands with Johanan. Azariah in 43:2 is also called Hoshaiah’s son.
people.jezaniah-hoshaiah.meaning: He comes with Johanan and all the people to Jeremiah. They ask him to pray that God will show them the way. They promise to obey, whether the answer is good or bad. The text does not say if he and Azariah are one man.
people.azariah-hoshaiah.relations: He is Hoshaiah’s son and speaks with Johanan. Jezaniah in 42:1 is also called Hoshaiah’s son.
people.azariah-hoshaiah.meaning: Jeremiah tells the people not to go to Egypt. Azariah tells him he speaks falsely. He says Baruch turned Jeremiah against them to hand them to the Chaldeans. The text does not say if he and Jezaniah are one man.
people.women-queen.role: Judean women in Egypt who burn incense to the queen of the sky
people.women-queen.relations: They say their husbands knew of the cakes and drink offerings.
people.women-queen.meaning: They and their husbands tell Jeremiah they will not listen to him. They say food was plenty when they burned incense to the queen of the sky. They say hunger and the sword came when they stopped. Jeremiah answers that the incense itself brought the disaster.
people.hophra.relations: Jeremiah sets him beside Zedekiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar took.
people.hophra.meaning: The people of Judah have gone to Egypt to be safe. God says he will give Hophra to enemies who seek his life. This will be the sign that God’s words against them stand.
people.necho.role: Egyptian king whose army is struck at Carchemish
people.necho.relations: His army faces Nebuchadnezzar by the river Euphrates.
people.necho.meaning: The message about Egypt opens with his army at Carchemish. Nebuchadnezzar strikes it in the fourth year of Jehoiakim. The verse says no more about Necoh himself.
people.seraiah-neriah.role: Official told to read Jeremiah’s Babylon scroll and sink it
people.seraiah-neriah.relations: He is the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah. Baruch is called by the same father and grandfather.
people.seraiah-neriah.meaning: He goes with King Zedekiah to Babylon in the king’s fourth year. Jeremiah gives him a scroll of all the evil coming on Babylon. He must read it there and tie a stone to it. Then he must throw it in the Euphrates. He must say that Babylon will sink the same way.
people.hamutal.role: Zedekiah’s mother, named in the last chapter
people.hamutal.relations: She is Zedekiah’s mother and the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
people.hamutal.meaning: The last chapter names her when it tells of Zedekiah’s reign. Her father is Jeremiah of Libnah. The prophet Jeremiah is from Anathoth, not Libnah. She does nothing in the story.
people.seraiah-priest.role: Chief priest taken and killed after Jerusalem falls
people.seraiah-priest.relations: Nebuzaradan takes him with Zephaniah the second priest. He is not Seraiah the son of Neriah.
people.seraiah-priest.meaning: Nebuzaradan takes him from the city with Zephaniah and three keepers of the threshold. He brings them to the king of Babylon at Riblah. The king puts them to death there.
people.solomon.role: Earlier king who made the temple’s bronze pieces
people.solomon.relations: The text says King Solomon made them for the LORD’s house.
people.solomon.meaning: The Chaldeans break up the bronze pillars, the sea, and the twelve bronze bulls. They carry the bronze to Babylon. The text says King Solomon had made these things. He does nothing else in this book.
people.evil-merodach.relations: He is king of Babylon and deals kindly with Jehoiachin.
people.evil-merodach.meaning: In his first year he lets Jehoiachin out of prison. He speaks kindly to him and gives him a seat above the other captive kings. He changes his prison clothes. He gives him food every day for the rest of his life.
places.jerusalem.summary: Jeremiah warns the city in the temple, at the gates, and in the king’s house. In chapter 39 Babylon’s army breaks in. In chapter 52 Nebuzaradan burns the temple and the houses.
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.anathoth.summary: Jeremiah comes from the priests of Anathoth (chapter 1). Men of Anathoth threaten his life in chapter 11. In chapter 32 he buys Hanamel’s field there.
places.anathoth.limits: More than one site has been proposed for Anathoth. The marker shows one general location.
places.babylon.summary: Nebuchadnezzar carries Jeconiah and many others here (chapter 24). Jeremiah sends the captives a letter in chapter 29. Chapters 50 and 51 say Babylon itself will fall.
places.babylon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.mizpah.summary: Gedaliah governs from Mizpah, and Jeremiah lives with him there (chapter 40). In chapter 41 Ishmael kills Gedaliah and takes the people away.
places.mizpah.limits: More than one site has been proposed for Mizpah. The marker shows one general location.
places.ramah.summary: In chapter 31 a voice in Ramah is Rachel weeping for her children. In chapter 40 Nebuzaradan frees Jeremiah from his chains at Ramah.
places.ramah.limits: More than one site has been proposed for Ramah. The marker shows one general location.
places.riblah.summary: Nebuchadnezzar judges Zedekiah here in chapters 39 and 52. He kills Zedekiah’s sons and puts out Zedekiah’s eyes. He also kills the chief priest Seraiah and other captives.
places.riblah.limits: The text places Riblah in the land of Hamath. The marker shows a proposed location.
places.jericho.summary: The Chaldean army catches Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. Chapters 39 and 52 both tell it.
places.jericho.limits: The text names the plains of Jericho, not one spot. The marker shows the town.
places.carchemish.summary: Pharaoh Necoh’s army stands at Carchemish by the river Euphrates. Nebuchadnezzar strikes it there (chapter 46).
places.carchemish.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.shiloh.summary: In chapters 7 and 26 God points the temple crowd to Shiloh. His place once stood there, and he says to see what he did to it. He says the temple in Jerusalem will become like it.
places.shiloh.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.samaria.summary: In chapter 23 God says Samaria’s prophets spoke by Baal. He then charges Jerusalem’s prophets with adultery and lies.
places.samaria.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.lachish.summary: In chapter 34 Babylon’s army fights against Lachish. Only Lachish and Azekah are left of Judah’s walled cities.
places.lachish.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.azekah.summary: In chapter 34 Babylon’s army fights against Azekah. Only Azekah and Lachish are left of Judah’s walled cities.
places.azekah.limits: The marker shows the traditional location.
places.gibeon.summary: Johanan finds Ishmael by the great waters in Gibeon (chapter 41). The captives turn back to Johanan, and Ishmael escapes with eight men.
places.gibeon.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.bethlehem.summary: Johanan’s group stays at Geruth Chimham, by Bethlehem, in chapter 41. They mean to go on to Egypt.
places.bethlehem.limits: The text names Geruth Chimham, a place by Bethlehem. The marker shows Bethlehem.
places.tyre.summary: In chapter 25 the kings of Tyre must drink the cup of God’s anger. In chapter 27 Jeremiah sends a yoke message to the king of Tyre. Chapter 47 says Tyre will lose every helper.
places.tyre.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.sidon.summary: In chapter 25 the kings of Sidon must drink the cup of God’s anger. In chapter 27 Jeremiah sends a yoke message to the king of Sidon. Chapter 47 says Sidon will lose every helper.
places.sidon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.gaza.summary: Chapter 47 speaks about the Philistines before Pharaoh strikes Gaza. It says baldness has come on Gaza.
places.gaza.limits: The marker shows the ancient city’s general location.
places.ashkelon.summary: Chapter 47 says Ashkelon is brought to nothing. The sword of the LORD is sent against Ashkelon and the seashore.
places.ashkelon.limits: The marker shows the ancient city’s general location.
places.heshbon.summary: In chapter 48 men in Heshbon plan evil against Moab. Fire also goes out from Heshbon. In chapter 49 Heshbon is told to wail.
places.heshbon.limits: More than one site has been proposed for Heshbon. The marker shows one general location.
places.rabbah.summary: In chapter 49 God says war will come to Rabbah of the children of Ammon. It will become an empty heap.
places.rabbah.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.damascus.summary: In chapter 49 Damascus grows weak and turns to run. God says he will light a fire in its wall.
places.damascus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.moab.summary: In chapter 25 Moab is among the nations that must drink the cup. Chapter 48 tells of its ruined towns and its grief. That chapter ends with a promise to bring Moab’s captives back.
places.moab.limits: The marker stands for a wide region. It does not mark ancient borders.
places.edom.summary: Edom is among the nations named in chapters 25 and 27. In chapter 49 God says its high rock homes will not save it.
places.edom.limits: The marker stands for a wide region. It does not mark ancient borders.
places.gilead.summary: In chapter 8 Jeremiah asks if there is no balm in Gilead for his people. In chapter 46 Egypt is told to get balm there, but nothing heals her.
places.gilead.limits: The marker stands for a wide region. It does not mark ancient borders.
places.egypt.summary: Uriah flees to Egypt and is brought back (chapter 26). Pharaoh’s army comes out and goes home in chapter 37. In chapter 43 Johanan’s group goes there against Jeremiah’s word. Chapter 46 warns Egypt itself.
places.egypt.limits: The marker stands for a wide region. It does not mark ancient borders.
places.tahpanhes.summary: Johanan’s group arrives here with Jeremiah and Baruch (chapter 43). Jeremiah hides great stones at the entry of Pharaoh’s house. He says Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne on them.
places.tahpanhes.limits: The marker shows the area of Tell Defenneh. The place of the hidden stones is not known.
places.memphis.summary: Chapter 2 says the children of Memphis have broken Israel’s crown. Jews live there in chapter 44. Chapter 46 says Memphis will be burned and left empty.
places.memphis.limits: The marker shows the ancient city’s general location.
places.hinnom.summary: In chapter 7 God charges Judah with burning children at Topheth in this valley. In chapter 19 Jeremiah takes elders there with a clay jar. God says it will be called the valley of Slaughter.
places.hinnom.limits: The marker shows the valley’s general location. The place of the altar is not known.
sources.web.limits: Chapter order is not a continuous timeline. A speaker’s claim stays with that speaker. Different people with the same name have separate profiles. Jeremiah 27:1 names Jehoiakim, but 27:3 and 27:12 name Zedekiah. The reading keeps this difference. Jezaniah in 42:1 and Azariah in 43:2 share Hoshaiah as father. The two names do not prove that they were two separate people. Nergal Sharezer occurs twice in 39:3. The group profile does not treat these officials as one person.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: Map points are estimates. A town marker does not prove that an event took place there.
sources.luther-jeremiah-summary.limits: This guide does not use the page’s broad claim about length. No verse note is credited to this overview.
sources.luther-jeremiah-background.limit: Its proposals about Baruch and later writers are not treated as settled. It dates Jerusalem’s fall to 587 BCE. Other reviewed sources use 586 BCE. Neither date is treated as settled. The Greek and Hebrew versions differ in length and order.
sources.mcclellan-queen.summary: The hosts discuss household offerings. They argue that the queen is Astarte.
sources.mcclellan-queen.limits: The captions do not reliably label speakers and may contain errors. The audio and the full episode were not reviewed. No caption wording is quoted. The program argues for Astarte, but Jeremiah does not give that name. The cited inscriptions and the full Ackerman book were not independently reviewed.
sources.ackerman-record.summary: Eerdmans, the publisher, confirms the book that Data Over Dogma cites.
sources.ackerman-record.limits: This record confirms only the book’s publication details. The full book and its inscriptions were not reviewed. Its claims are not presented as evidence that was independently examined.
sources.redditt-record.summary: Eerdmans confirms the author, title, ISBN, and date of a book cited by Wikipedia.
sources.redditt-record.limits: The full book and cited pages 132–33 were not reviewed. This record confirms publication, not what the book says about any chapter.
sources.wiki-jeremiah.limits: This page was used for an overview and to find books. Reader notes use scripture and reviewed primary material. Its book list has a mismatched Kugler and Hartin title, which is not used here.
sources.cfm-jeremiah-1.limits: Linked talks were not separately reviewed. The lesson applies the fishers and hunters to missionary work. Jeremiah 16:16–18 uses them for a pursuit, and the two uses stay apart. The study questions for each passage are original.
sources.lds-jeremiah-helps.limits: The manual’s outside references and linked talks were not independently read. Its reading of the new covenant and the righteous Branch stays in the LDS lens. Jeremiah’s death in Egypt is a belief, not an event stated in this book.
sources.openbible-jeremiah-geo.limits: This is an open list of places, not archaeological proof of the events. Its map points are estimates. Rival site proposals remain uncertain. No index photographs are copied.
chapters.*.mapNote: Points show the places this chapter names. A line joins two places when the text gives both ends of a trip.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The chapter names places but gives no trip between them. The map draws no line.
chapters.29.routeEvidence: Jeremiah 29:1–3 says Elasah and Gemariah carry the letter from Jerusalem to Babylon. The text does not name the roads between.
chapters.39.routeEvidence: Jeremiah 39:4–7 follows Zedekiah from Jerusalem to Jericho, Riblah, and then toward Babylon. The lines join rough points, not known roads.
chapters.40.routeEvidence: Jeremiah 40:1–6 puts Jeremiah at Ramah, then with Gedaliah at Mizpah. The road and both sites are uncertain.
chapters.52.routeEvidence: Jeremiah 52:7–11 tells Zedekiah’s flight again: Jericho, Riblah, then Babylon. The text does not name the roads.
